text:
maria: ACME follow-up: they want a small, contract-backed "grace SLO" for Dedicated pools — accept very short spikes with explicit cost/leakage controls. Can we carve an MVP that is safe for pools and clear for billing?

krish: TL;DR proposal: grace_slo = tenant opt-in flag + two knobs (window_s, token_limit) + demotion_order. Keep scope strictly pool-local. Objective: accept requests <= token_limit for up to window_s, then revert to normal quota.

dan: Ops caveat: must prevent cross-tenant contagion. If many tenants use grace_slo simultaneously, pool pressure spikes. Add pool-level budget and automatic backoff. Also prefer routing to prewarmed quantized workers rather than weight-swap to reduce thrash.

krish: Example config for RFC:```yaml
tenant_quota:
  max_concurrent: 100
  grace_slo:
    enabled: true
    window_s: 12
    token_limit: 800
    demotion_order: ["rwd-3b-quant","rwd-1b","reject"]
    bill_behavior: "bill_actual_with_demote_tag"
    scope: "tenant_pool_only"
```

olivia: From product/launch side: acceptance criteria: 1) pilot with ACME + 2 internal tenants for 10 days, 2) telemetry shows demotion_rate < 0.5% and demoted p95 latency within 1.5x of baseline, 3) billing emits demotion events and invoice sample, 4) docs + opt-out API.

finance-bot: finance: agree but require demotion tagging for billing reconciliation (`demoted=true` on usage lines). Also want a demo invoice showing demoted-charge vs base-charge during pilot.

dan: Runtime checklist: - local demotion first (in-worker quantized) - route to prewarmed quantized worker if memory prevents swap - prewarm policy: default 6% pool buffer per tenant opt-in - pool budget: cap aggregate grace allocations to 8% of pool or disable across pool - circuit: suspend grace for 5m if pool_demote_rate > 1% and regional RPC latency > 10% rise

krish: Telemetry events: `grace_accept`, `grace_demote(tenant,orig,demoted,tokens)`, `grace_reject` + `grace_backoff` at pool-level. Alerts: `grace_contagion` when demote_rate & latency rise together.

olivia: Product copy for customers: "When enabled, Grace SLO lets short bursts be accepted using lower-capacity model variants to preserve availability. Outputs may differ; Redwood will tag demoted requests on invoices and run automated QA during pilots." Simple and transparent.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: branch `grace_slo_v1` created. Canary dry-run scheduled: prod-canary 2024-11-07T18:00Z (flagged).

maria: Next steps: krish to write short RFC with memory/prewarm numbers and failure modes, dan to draft ops runbook & circuit settings, olivia to prepare pilot acceptance template and customer-facing wording, finance to prepare invoice sample. Meeting Thursday 9am to finalize. :thumbsup:
